question: Can a bounded density-dependent interimage development operator recover known cross-layer suppression that independent characteristic curves and a fixed post-density affine matrix cannot explain on held exposure groups?
claim_ceiling: generic-physical-inspired synthetic known-operator representation evidence only; no stock, process, calibrated response, real-film operator or product claim

operator.name: positive-cross-layer-log-exposure-suppression-v1
operator.coupling_constraints: A has zero diagonal and finite nonnegative off-diagonal entries bounded by 0.8

baselines: known independent per-layer curves with zero coupling
known independent curves followed by one fitted unconstrained affine density map

research_basis.source: Hanson and Horton, Subtractive Color Reproduction: Interimage Effects, JOSA 42(9), 1952
research_basis.use: equation-level precedent that dye image density depends on multiple layer exposures; no parameter calibration

research_basis.source: Wychorski, Interimage Effects in Various Subtractive Color Materials, RIT, 1976
research_basis.use: experimental precedent that combined-layer development changes characteristic curves; no reusable measurements
manufacturer-level subtractive dye and colour-film process context; no stock recipe

forbidden_fallbacks: fit or retune any parameter on the sealed 71-pair AO9 display-proxy pool
change witnesses, seeds, controls, thresholds or exposure groups after confirmatory output
fit base characteristic curves jointly with coupling in this pilot
use photograph content, scanner identity or source identity as an input
call synthetic recovery a measured interimage effect, stock response, push/pull mode or calibrated film operator
advance to photographs if any automatic gate fails

branch_rule.pass: retain the explicit density-dependent interimage representation as a generic physical-inspired mechanism and seek new controlled single-layer plus neutral sensitometry before any real fit
branch_rule.fail: close this parameterization without modifying the existing P2/P7/AO6 champions
